destination.name: Apia
destination.tagline: Samoa's easygoing capital and harbour base for Upolu's reefs, falls and history
destination.description: Apia is Samoa's capital, on the north coast of Upolu, with about 42,000 people. It is small and a little worn, and most visitors use it to get their bearings and plan trips around the island. In town the clock tower war memorial marks the centre, and Robert Louis Stevenson's house at Vailima lies 5 km south. In 1889 seven German, American and British warships refused to leave the harbour as a typhoon approached, and all but one were lost.
whyVisit: Snorkel the reef at Palolo Deep
Base yourself for Upolu day trips

goodToKnow.title: Check the Palolo Deep tide
goodToKnow.detail: At low tide you paddle over sharp coral to reach deep water. Read the tide chart at the gate and swim out on the incoming tide.

goodToKnow.title: Sunday is a rest day
goodToKnow.detail: Most shops and businesses close and you should not walk through villages. Dress modestly, with knee-length shorts away from the beach.

goodToKnow.title: Mind dogs after dusk
goodToKnow.detail: Free-roaming dogs are common in Apia in the evening. Most ignore you, and walking in from the suburbs after dark is best avoided.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Apia is driest in {months}, well clear of the October to March rainy and cyclone season.
